name: Boston Consulting Group
one_liner: MBB firm known for pioneering strategy concepts, a strong digital and AI build arm (BCG X), and conversational, candidate-driven case interviews.
at_a_glance: About 33,500 employees and 100+ offices in 50+ countries (2025).
Reported roughly $14.4B revenue in 2025, its 22nd straight year of growth.
Tech and AI-related work now exceeds ~40% of revenue.

rounds: Screen: some candidates complete an online case (Casey chatbot) depending on office and program.
First round: ~2 case interviews, each with some behavioral discussion.
Final round: ~2-3 case interviews with senior leaders, plus fit questions.
interview_process.case_style: Conversational and largely candidate-driven: structure the problem, ask for data, analyze charts, do quick math, and land a recommendation. Cases can feel less scripted than McKinsey's.
interview_process.fit_style: Behavioral questions woven into case interviews; BCG lists integrity, intellectual curiosity, creative thinking, collaborative mindset, and drive as qualities it looks for.
interview_process.assessments: Online case assessment used in many geographies (Casey chatbot plus quantitative questions), office-dependent. BCG also offers OneDay@BCG, a free job simulation.

what_they_look_for: Creative thinking and insight beyond the obvious
culture: Known for intellectual rigor and 'unconventional' thinking rooted in founder Bruce Henderson's legacy.
Rapidly growing BCG X tech-and-build arm means more mixed consultant-engineer teams.
Relatively flexible, less standardized approach than McKinsey; strong emphasis on people development.
why_us_angles: Which BCG frameworks or Henderson Institute ideas shaped how you think about strategy?
How could BCG X's build-and-scale model use any product or tech experience you have?
Which BCG practice (e.g., consumer, tech, operations) connects to your background, and what have you learned from BCGers?
What would working on AI-driven transformations at BCG let you do that other firms would not?
prep_tips: Practice the Casey format: typed answers, predefined steps, and short recorded video summaries under time pressure.
Drive cases yourself: propose a structure, prioritize branches, and ask for the data you need.
Bring creative, insight-driven ideas, not just textbook frameworks.
Prepare crisp fit stories mapped to curiosity, collaboration, and drive.
Use BCG's case interview prep page and OneDay@BCG simulation to calibrate.
